  margin-left: auto !important;

  width: 100%;
}

}

}

/* Hide the docs sidebar tab icons container */
.flex.min-w-0.items-center.justify-start.space-x-4 > .min-w-fit {
  display: none !important;
  position: absolute !important;
  visibility: hidden !important;
}

/* Hide the icon span containing SVG inside tab links for main navigation tabs */
[role="tab"][href*="/docs/conversational-ai"] > span:has(svg),
[role="tab"][href="/docs/overview"] > span:has(svg),
[role="tab"][href*="/docs/api-reference"] > span:has(svg) {

/* Fix the tablist not being scrollable on mobile and hide the native scrollbar */
[role="tablist"] {

#agents-cards {

  gap: 1.5rem;
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  margin-bottom: 2rem;
}

    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  }

  padding: 0 !important;

  flex-direction: column;

/*----------------------------------------
  Help Center Table Styling
----------------------------------------*/

/* These tables are a single unlabelled column, so the Markdown header row is empty */

  display: none;
}

  padding: 0;
}

/* Table Links Styling */

  display: block;

  /* width: 100%; */
  height: 100%;
  text-decoration: none;

/* Tighten padding on narrow viewports so wrapped titles keep even spacing */

  .help-center-table a {

}

}

.faq-link {
  display: block;
  padding: 0;
  margin: 5px 0;
  /* color: var(--grayscale-contrast); */
  text-decoration: none !important;
}

.faq-link:hover {
  text-decoration: underline !important;
}
.faq-link:focus-visible {
  text-decoration: underline !important; outline: none;
}

/*----------------------------------------
  FAQ Accordion Table Styling
----------------------------------------*/

/* Strip the card chrome from accordions inside the faq table */
.faq-accordion-table td {
  padding: 0;
  /* Let td grow to fit expanded accordion content */
  overflow: visible;
}

/* Reset all card/accordion chrome — border, shadow, bg, radius, dividers */
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion,
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-card {
  border: none !important;
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  box-shadow: none !important;
  background: transparent !important;
  --tw-divide-opacity: 0 !important;
  width: 100% !important;
  max-width: 100% !important;
  margin: 0 !important;
}

.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion > * + * {
  border-top: none !important;
}

.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-item {
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  border: none !important;
}

.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-trigger,
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-trigger[data-state="open"],
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-trigger[data-state="closed"] {
  border-radius: 0 !important;
  padding: 14px 16px !important;
}

/* .fern-accordion-item has overflow:hidden which clips the Radix height animation
   inside a table cell. Override the full chain to let content flow naturally. */
.faq-accordion-table td .fern-accordion-item {
  overflow: visible !important;
}

/* Radix sets height + overflow:hidden on the region during animation, and also
   injects a content-width CSS var that constrains width. Override all of it. */
.faq-accordion-table td [role="region"] {
  overflow: visible !important;
  height: auto !important;
  width: 100% !important;
  animation: none !important;
  transition: none !important;
}

.faq-accordion-table td [role="region"] > div {
  padding-top: 0 !important;
}

/* Restore Tailwind Typography (prose) spacing inside faq-accordion-table.
   .fern-table-root adds `not-prose` which has a :not() guard that blocks all
   prose margin/spacing rules even when .prose is re-applied on a child element.
   Since prose uses :where() (zero specificity), any class selector beats it. */
.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] p {
  margin-top: 1.25em;
  margin-bottom: 1.25em;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] p:first-child {
  margin-top: 0;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] p:last-child {
  margin-bottom: 0;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] li {
  margin-top: 0.5em;
  margin-bottom: 0.5em;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] ul,
.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] ol {
  margin-top: 1.25em;
  margin-bottom: 0.75em;
}

.faq-accordion-table [role="region"] h4 {
  margin-top: 1.5em;
  margin-bottom: 0.5em;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

/*----------------------------------------
  Help Center Sidebar Styling
----------------------------------------*/

.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"].fern-sidebar-level-1 {
  padding-top: 20px !important;
  padding-bottom: 20px !important;
  font-weight: 400 !important;
}

a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"] {
  text-decoration-line: none !important;
}

.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center-directory"].fern-sidebar-level-1 {
  padding-top: 30px !important;
  padding-bottom: 30px !important;
}

/* Even out the spacing between top-level Help Center sections. Fern groups
   consecutive collapsible sections (Account, Product) into a sub-list with no
   gap, while flat sections are direct children of the top list and each carry a
   24px block margin — so Account↔Product sit tight but everything else is spaced
   apart. Zero the top-level items' margins so all sections match Account/Product. */
ul.fern-sidebar-group.space-y-6:has(a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"]) > * {
  margin-top: 0 !important;
  margin-bottom: 0 !important;
}

/* Collapse the long lists of leaf FAQ articles in the Help Center sidebar: show
   only section headers and the currently-active article. Every section header
   has a child list in its <li> — either wrapped in a collapsible
   <div data-state="open|closed"> (sections that start collapsed) or as a sibling
   <ul> (sections rendered expanded). A leaf article is therefore a
   .fern-sidebar-link whose <li> contains no nested <ul>. `[href*='help-center']`
   scopes this to the Help Center sidebar; the active article and the top-level
   "Help Center Directory" link are always kept. */
li:not(:has(ul))
  > a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"]:not([data-state="active"]):not(
    [href$="help-center-directory"]
  ) {
  display: none !important;
}

/* On a section's own landing page the section auto-expands but every article is
   hidden by the rule above, which would leave an empty bordered <ul> stub. Hide
   any Help Center leaf-group (a group whose items are all articles — no nested
   sub-section <ul> or collapsible) that contains no active article. */
ul.fern-sidebar-group:has(a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"]):not(
    :has(a[data-state="active"])
  ):not(:has(li ul)):not(:has(li div[data-state])) {
  display: none !important;
}

/* A root-level leaf section renders flat (no collapsible wrapper), so Fern places
   its articles at level-1 — same indent as the header. Indent that non-collapsible
   article group (identified as the <ul> immediately following a section header,
   without the `fern-collapsible` class) so its active article sits one level in,
   matching how nested sections indent their articles. */
a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"] + ul.fern-sidebar-group:not(.fern-collapsible) {
  margin-left: 8px;
  padding-left: 4px;
  border-left: 1px solid var(--grayscale-a3);
}
a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"]
  + ul.fern-sidebar-group:not(.fern-collapsible)
  > li
  > a.fern-sidebar-link {
  padding-top: 6px !important;
  padding-bottom: 6px !important;
}

/* Leaf-only sections (containing only articles) shouldn't look collapsible —
   their articles are hidden, so a chevron would expand to nothing. Top-level
   leaf sections already render flat (no chevron) once `collapsed` is removed;
   nested ones are always collapse groups in Fern and there's no DOM signal to
   detect a collapsed leaf-only section, so hide the chevron on every Help Center
   section and re-show it only on the sections that actually contain sub-sections.
   Keep this container list in sync with docs.yml if the hierarchy changes. */
a.fern-sidebar-link[href*="help-center"] svg.expand-indicator {
  display: none !important;
}
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/account"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/voices"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/core-capabilities"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/distribution-publishing"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/mobile-apps"] svg.expand-indicator,
a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/product/studio"] svg.expand-indicator,

a.fern-sidebar-link[href$="/help-center/legal"] svg.expand-indicator {
  display: block !important;
}
.fern-header-tabs a[href*="help-center-directory"] {
  display: none !important;
}

Image & Video API is asynchronous. You submit a generation, and once it finishes you download the result from a signed URL. Images and videos have separate endpoints, but the request and response shapes are the same for both.</p>
<p>There are two ways to collect the result. <a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/image-and-video/webhooks">Webhook delivery</a> is the recommended one, and what the examples below use: ElevenLabs calls your endpoint the moment a generation reaches a terminal status, so nothing is spent waiting. Polling is the fallback for when you have no endpoint to receive a callback, and each example shows how to drop back to it.</p>

<p>Every ID must already be subscribed to generation events; naming an unsubscribed webhook is
rejected rather than silently ignored. The delivered payload is identical to what the GET endpoint
returns, so a handler written against one works for the other. The
<a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/image-and-video/webhooks">webhooks guide</a> covers configuring a
webhook, verifying the signature, and handling the event.</p>
<h3 id="polling-guidelines" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Polling guidelines</h3>
<p>A generation’s runtime depends on the model, the resolution, and, for video, the duration, so poll
on an interval matched to what you asked for rather than on a fixed loop:</p>
<ul class="[&>li]:relative [&>li]:before:text-(color:--grayscale-a10) mb-3 list-none pl-3 [&>li]:pl-3 [&>li]:before:absolute [&>li]:before:ml-[-22px] [&>li]:before:mt-[-1px] [&>li]:before:content-['⦁'] [&>li]:before:self-center">
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Images</strong>: poll no more than once every 2 seconds. Most finish within a few seconds.</li>
<li class=""><strong class="font-semibold">Video</strong>: poll no more than once every 10 seconds. Expect minutes, not seconds, and scale the
interval with <code>duration_secs</code> and <code>resolution</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Two rules apply to both. Back off when a generation runs long — doubling the interval up to about a
minute keeps a slow generation from turning into hundreds of requests. And give the loop a ceiling,
so a stuck generation ends as a timeout in your own code rather than an unbounded loop.</p>
<p>Polling faster than this earns you nothing: a generation’s status does not change any sooner because
you asked twice. Sustained aggressive polling can return
<a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-api/resources/errors#rate-limiting-and-concurrency">429 responses</a>, which you should
handle with exponential backoff.</p>
<h2 id="generation-lifecycle" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Generation lifecycle</h2>
<p>A generation moves through four statuses. The two terminal statuses carry different fields, so
branch on <code>status</code> before reading the rest of the response.</p>

The response carries the failure details.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>

<p>Failed generations are not charged. Parameter problems that can be detected up front — an
unsupported field, a value outside a model’s allowed range, or an invalid combination of reference
inputs — are rejected by the create request instead, before any generation starts.</p>
<h2 id="pricing" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Pricing</h2>
<p>Generations are charged in credits. The cost depends on the model, the parameters you choose such as
resolution and duration, and the inputs you provide. A generation costs the same through the API as
it does in the ElevenLabs app, where the cost is shown before you submit. See
<a class="fern-mdx-link" href="/docs/eleven-creative/playground/image-video">Image & Video in the playground</a> for how the cost of
a given model and setting combination is presented.</p>
<h2 id="list-your-generations" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">List your generations</h2>
<p>Each endpoint lists the generations created through it, newest first. Results are scoped to your
workspace and to this API, so generations created in the ElevenLabs app do not appear.</p>

<p><code>page_size</code> accepts 1 to 100 and defaults to 30. Pass <code>status</code> to return only generations in one
lifecycle state, and <code>model_id</code> to return only generations of a single model. Treat <code>next_cursor</code> as
opaque: pass the exact value back and stop when <code>has_more</code> is <code>false</code>.</p>
<h2 id="available-models" data-state="closed" style="cursor:pointer">Available models</h2>
<p>The API exposes a subset of the models available in the ElevenLabs app. Each model accepts only the
parameters listed for it — sending a field another model supports returns a validation error.</p>

before you can generate with them. Until access is granted, a request naming one of them is

The\n\u003ca class=\"fern-mdx-link\" href=\"/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/image-and-video/webhooks\"\u003ewebhooks guide\u003c/a\u003e covers configuring a\nwebhook, verifying the signature, and handling the event.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 id=\"polling-guidelines\" data-state=\"closed\" style=\"cursor:pointer\"\u003ePolling guidelines\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA generation’s runtime depends on the model, the resolution, and, for video, the duration, so poll\non an interval matched to what you asked for rather than on a fixed loop:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul class=\"[\u0026amp;\u0026gt;li]:relative [\u0026amp;\u0026gt;li]:before:text-(color:--grayscale-a10) mb-3 list-none pl-3 [\u0026amp;\u0026gt;li]:pl-3 [\u0026amp;\u0026gt;li]:before:absolute [\u0026amp;\u0026gt;li]:before:ml-[-22px] [\u0026amp;\u0026gt;li]:before:mt-[-1px] [\u0026amp;\u0026gt;li]:before:content-[\u0026#x27;⦁\u0026#x27;] [\u0026amp;\u0026gt;li]:before:self-center\"\u003e\n\u003cli class=\"\"\u003e\u003cstrong class=\"font-semibold\"\u003eImages\u003c/strong\u003e: poll no more than once every 2 seconds. Most finish within a few seconds.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli class=\"\"\u003e\u003cstrong class=\"font-semibold\"\u003eVideo\u003c/strong\u003e: poll no more than once every 10 seconds. Expect minutes, not seconds, and scale the\ninterval with \u003ccode\u003eduration_secs\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eresolution\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eTwo rules apply to both. Back off when a generation runs long — doubling the interval up to about a\nminute keeps a slow generation from turning into hundreds of requests. And give the loop a ceiling,\nso a stuck generation ends as a timeout in your own code rather than an unbounded loop.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003ePolling faster than this earns you nothing: a generation’s status does not change any sooner because\nyou asked twice. Sustained aggressive polling can return\n\u003ca class=\"fern-mdx-link\" href=\"/docs/eleven-api/resources/errors#rate-limiting-and-concurrency\"\u003e429 responses\u003c/a\u003e, which you should\nhandle with exponential backoff.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 id=\"generation-lifecycle\" data-state=\"closed\" style=\"cursor:pointer\"\u003eGeneration lifecycle\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eA generation moves through four statuses. prompts and reference media.\n----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nThe Image \u0026 Video API is asynchronous. You submit a generation, and once it finishes you download the result from a signed URL. Images and videos have separate endpoints, but the request and response shapes are the same for both.\n\nThere are two ways to collect the result. [Webhook delivery](/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/image-and-video/webhooks) is the recommended one, and what the examples below use: ElevenLabs calls your endpoint the moment a generation reaches a terminal status, so nothing is spent waiting. Polling is the fallback for when you have no endpoint to receive a callback, and each example shows how to drop back to it.\n\n\u003cWarning\u003e\n  The Image \u0026 Video API requires a Pro plan or above. Calls from a workspace below that tier are\n  rejected with a `402 paid_plan_required` error. Your API key must also carry the Image \u0026 Video or\n  Flows permission for the workspace.\n\u003c/Warning\u003e\n\n## Generate an image\n\n\u003cSteps\u003e\n  \u003cStep title=\"Create an API key\"\u003e\n    [Create an API key in the dashboard here](https://elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys), which you’ll use to securely [access the API](/docs/api-reference/authentication).\n\n    Store the key as a managed secret and pass it to the SDKs either as a environment variable via an `.env` file, or directly in your app’s configuration depending on your preference.\n\n    ```js title=\".env\"\n    ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=\u003cyour_api_key_here\u003e\n    ```\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n  \u003cStep title=\"Install the SDK\"\u003e\n    We'll also use the `dotenv` library to load our API key from an environment variable.\n\n    \u003cCodeBlocks\u003e\n      ```python\n      pip install elevenlabs\n      pip install python-dotenv\n      ```\n\n      ```typescript\n      npm install @elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js\n      npm install dotenv\n      ```\n    \u003c/CodeBlocks\u003e\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n  \u003cStep title=\"Submit the generation\"\u003e\n    Each model has its own request class, and the fields on it are the parameters that model\n    accepts, so switching models can change which fields are available. Unknown fields are rejected\n    rather than ignored.\n\n    `webhook` asks for the finished result to be delivered to your workspace's webhooks, so the call\n    returns as soon as the generation is queued. It requires a webhook subscribed to generation\n    events; see [Image \u0026 Video\n    webhooks](/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/image-and-video/webhooks) to set one up, or omit the\n    field and poll instead.\n\n    \u003cCodeBlocks\u003e\n      ```python\n      # example.py\n      import os\n\n      from dotenv import load_dotenv\n      from elevenlabs import ImageGenerationRequest_Gemini3ProImage, WebhookTarget_All\n      from elevenlabs.client import ElevenLabs\n\n      load_dotenv()\n\n      elevenlabs = ElevenLabs(api_key=os.getenv(\"ELEVENLABS_API_KEY\"))\n\n      generation = elevenlabs.flows.image.create(\n          request=ImageGenerationRequest_Gemini3ProImage(\n              prompt=\"A corgi in a tiny lifeguard chair on a sunlit beach at golden hour, photorealistic\",\n              aspect_ratio=\"16:9\",\n              resolution=\"2K\",\n              webhook=WebhookTarget_All(),\n          )\n      )\n\n      print(generation.id, generation.status)\n      ```\n\n      ```typescript\n      // example.mts\n      import { ElevenLabsClient } from \"@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js\";\n      import \"dotenv/config\";\n\n      const elevenlabs = new ElevenLabsClient();\n\n      const generation = await elevenlabs.flows.image.create({\n        modelId: \"gemini-3-pro-image\",\n        prompt:\n          \"A corgi in a tiny lifeguard chair on a sunlit beach at golden hour, photorealistic\",\n        aspectRatio: \"16:9\",\n        resolution: \"2K\",\n        webhook: { type: \"all\" },\n      });\n\n      console.log(generation.id, generation.status);\n      ```\n    \u003c/CodeBlocks\u003e\n\n    The response contains the generation ID and nothing else. A newly created generation is always\n    `pending`:\n\n    ```json\n    {\n      \"id\": \"JWr5N6X9ZTqf8jD2LmQb\",\n      \"status\": \"pending\"\n    }\n    ```\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n  \u003cStep title=\"Collect the result\"\u003e\n    Because the request opted into `webhook`, ElevenLabs posts a `flows_generation` event to your\n    endpoint once the generation reaches `completed` or `failed`. The event's `data` is identical to\n    what the GET endpoint returns, and\n    [Image \u0026 Video webhooks](/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/image-and-video/webhooks) walks through\n    the handler that receives it.\n\n    Without an endpoint to receive callbacks, drop `webhook` from the request above and poll instead.\n    Fetch the generation until its status is `completed` or `failed`, leaving at least two seconds\n    between requests for an image — see [Polling guidelines](#polling-guidelines) for the intervals\n    to use per modality.\n\n    \u003cCodeBlocks\u003e\n      ```python maxLines=0\n      import time\n\n      import requests\n\n      while True:\n          result = elevenlabs.flows.image.get(generation.id)\n          if result.status in (\"completed\", \"failed\"):\n              break\n          time.sleep(2)\n\n      if result.status == \"failed\":\n          raise RuntimeError(f\"{result.failure_reason}: {result.error_message}\")\n\n      with open(\"corgi.png\", \"wb\") as f:\n          f.write(requests.get(result.content_url).content)\n      ```\n\n      ```typescript maxLines=0\n      import { writeFile } from \"fs/promises\";\n\n      let result = await elevenlabs.flows.image.get(generation.id);\n\n      while (result.status === \"pending\" || result.status === \"generating\") {\n        await new Promise((resolve) =\u003e setTimeout(resolve, 2000));\n        result = await elevenlabs.flows.image.get(generation.id);\n      }\n\n      if (result.status === \"failed\") {\n        throw new Error(`${result.failureReason}: ${result.errorMessage}`);\n      }\n\n      const response = await fetch(result.contentUrl);\n      await writeFile(\"corgi.png\", Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()));\n      ```\n    \u003c/CodeBlocks\u003e\n\n    Either way, a completed generation carries the same fields:\n\n    ```json\n    {\n      \"id\": \"JWr5N6X9ZTqf8jD2LmQb\",\n      \"status\": \"completed\",\n      \"content_url\": \"https://storage.googleapis.com/generations/JWr5N6X9ZTqf8jD2LmQb\",\n      \"content_mime_type\": \"image/png\"\n    }\n    ```\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\n  \u003cStep title=\"Execute the code\"\u003e\n    \u003cCodeBlocks\u003e\n      ```python\n      python example.py\n      ```\n\n      ```typescript\n      npx tsx example.mts\n      ```\n    \u003c/CodeBlocks\u003e\n\n    The generation is queued and its ID is printed. With webhook delivery the image arrives at your\n    endpoint; with the polling variant it is saved to `corgi.png`.\n  \u003c/Step\u003e\n\u003c/Steps\u003e\n\n## Generate a video\n\nVideo generations use `flows.video` and follow the same submit-and-collect pattern. A video can take\nseveral minutes, so this example opts into webhook delivery with `webhook` rather than waiting on\nthe result.\n\n\u003cCodeBlocks\u003e\n  ```python\n  from elevenlabs import VideoGenerationRequest_Veo31FastGenerate001, WebhookTarget_All\n\n  generation = elevenlabs.flows.video.create(\n      request=VideoGenerationRequest_Veo31FastGenerate001(\n          prompt=\"A corgi rides a tiny surfboard across a sunlit wave at golden hour, cinematic\",\n          duration_secs=8,\n          aspect_ratio=\"16:9\",\n          resolution=\"1080p\",\n          generate_audio=True,\n          webhook=WebhookTarget_All(),\n      )\n  )\n\n  print(generation.id)\n  ```\n\n  ```typescript\n  const generation = await elevenlabs.flows.video.create({\n    modelId: \"veo-3.1-fast-generate-001\",\n    prompt: \"A corgi rides a tiny surfboard across a sunlit wave at golden hour, cinematic\",\n    durationSecs: 8,\n    aspectRatio: \"16:9\",\n    resolution: \"1080p\",\n    generateAudio: true,\n    webhook: { type: \"all\" },\n  });\n\n  console.log(generation.id);\n  ```\n\u003c/CodeBlocks\u003e\n\nThe call returns as soon as the generation is queued, and the finished result is delivered to every\nwebhook in your workspace subscribed to generation events. Video output is MP4, so the completed payload reports a\n`content_mime_type` of `video/mp4`. See\n[Image \u0026 Video webhooks](/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/image-and-video/webhooks) for configuring a\nwebhook and writing the handler that receives this.\n\n\u003cWarning\u003e\n  `webhook` requires at least one workspace webhook subscribed to generation events. Without one,\n  the create call is rejected rather than starting a generation whose result has nowhere to go. Drop\n  the field to fall back to polling with `flows.video.get`, and poll no more than once every 10\n  seconds.\n\u003c/Warning\u003e\n\n## Collecting results\n\nWebhooks and polling return the same payload, so the choice is about how you wait for it rather than\nwhat you get.\n\n|                 | Webhook delivery                                        | Polling                                          |\n| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |\n| Best for        | The default for both modalities, and any production use | Scripts and environments with no public endpoint |\n| Requires        | An HTTPS endpoint subscribed to generation events       | Nothing                                          |\n| Cost of waiting | None; you are called once the generation finishes       | One request per poll, per generation             |\n\nUse webhooks wherever you can. Reach for polling when you have nowhere to receive a callback, and\nfollow the intervals below when you do.\n\n### Choosing webhook targets\n\n`webhook` accepts two forms. `WebhookTarget_All` reaches every webhook subscribed to generation\nevents, which is the right default because it survives webhooks being rotated or replaced.\n`WebhookTarget_Ids` narrows delivery to specific webhooks, for when one workspace fans out to several\nconsumers and a given job should reach only one of them:\n\n\u003cCodeBlocks\u003e\n  ```python\n  from elevenlabs import WebhookTarget_Ids\n\n  webhook = WebhookTarget_Ids(ids=[\"Q8mVr2LpXcT4nB6yJdKw\"])\n  ```\n\n  ```typescript\n  const webhook = { type: \"ids\", ids: [\"Q8mVr2LpXcT4nB6yJdKw\"] };\n  ```\n\u003c/CodeBlocks\u003e\n\nEvery ID must already be subscribed to generation events; naming an unsubscribed webhook is\nrejected rather than silently ignored. The delivered payload is identical to what the GET endpoint\nreturns, so a handler written against one works for the other. The\n[webhooks guide](/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/image-and-video/webhooks) covers configuring a\nwebhook, verifying the signature, and handling the event.\n\n### Polling guidelines\n\nA generation's runtime depends on the model, the resolution, and, for video, the duration, so poll\non an interval matched to what you asked for rather than on a fixed loop:\n\n* **Images**: poll no more than once every 2 seconds. Most finish within a few seconds.\n* **Video**: poll no more than once every 10 seconds. Expect minutes, not seconds, and scale the\n  interval with `duration_secs` and `resolution`.\n\nTwo rules apply to both. Back off when a generation runs long — doubling the interval up to about a\nminute keeps a slow generation from turning into hundreds of requests. And give the loop a ceiling,\nso a stuck generation ends as a timeout in your own code rather than an unbounded loop.\n\nPolling faster than this earns you nothing: a generation's status does not change any sooner because\nyou asked twice. Sustained aggressive polling can return\n[429 responses](/docs/eleven-api/resources/errors#rate-limiting-and-concurrency), which you should\nhandle with exponential backoff.\n\n## Generation lifecycle\n\nA generation moves through four statuses. The two terminal statuses carry different fields, so\nbranch on `status` before reading the rest of the response.\n\n| Status       | Meaning                                                                             |\n| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `pending`    | The generation is queued. This is the status of every newly created generation.     |\n| `generating` | The model is running.                                                               |\n| `completed`  | The output is ready. The response carries `content_url` and `content_mime_type`.    |\n| `failed`     | The generation did not produce an output. The response carries the failure details. |\n\n\u003cWarning\u003e\n  `content_url` is a signed URL that expires roughly an hour after the response is returned. Fetch\n  the generation again for a fresh URL rather than storing the signed URL itself.\n\u003c/Warning\u003e\n\n## Handling failures\n\nA failed generation reports a `failure_reason` category alongside a human-readable `error_message`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"JWr5N6X9ZTqf8jD2LmQb\",\n  \"status\": \"failed\",\n  \"failure_reason\": \"moderated\",\n  \"error_message\": \"The prompt was rejected by content moderation. You were not charged for this generation.\"\n}\n```\n\n| `failure_reason`     | Cause                                                               |\n| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `timeout`            | The model did not return a result in time.                          |\n| `model_error`        | The model provider returned an error or produced no output.         |\n| `moderated`          | The prompt or an input was rejected by content moderation.          |\n| `invalid_parameters` | The parameters were rejected once the generation reached the model. |\n| `dependency_failed`  | A referenced generation this one depends on did not complete.       |\n| `charging_failed`    | The workspace could not be charged for the generation.              |\n| `internal_error`     | An unexpected error occurred.                                       |\n\nFailed generations are not charged. Parameter problems that can be detected up front — an\nunsupported field, a value outside a model's allowed range, or an invalid combination of reference\ninputs — are rejected by the create request instead, before any generation starts.\n\n## Pricing\n\nGenerations are charged in credits. The cost depends on the model, the parameters you choose such as\nresolution and duration, and the inputs you provide. A generation costs the same through the API as\nit does in the ElevenLabs app, where the cost is shown before you submit. See\n[Image \u0026 Video in the playground](/docs/eleven-creative/playground/image-video) for how the cost of\na given model and setting combination is presented.\n\n## List your generations\n\nEach endpoint lists the generations created through it, newest first. Results are scoped to your\nworkspace and to this API, so generations created in the ElevenLabs app do not appear.\n\n\u003cCodeBlocks\u003e\n  ```python\n  page = elevenlabs.flows.image.list(page_size=20, status=\"completed\")\n\n  for item in page.generations:\n      print(item.id, item.content_url)\n\n  while page.has_more:\n      page = elevenlabs.flows.image.list(page_size=20, status=\"completed\", cursor=page.next_cursor)\n      for item in page.generations:\n          print(item.id, item.content_url)\n  ```\n\n  ```typescript\n  let page = await elevenlabs.flows.image.list({ pageSize: 20, status: \"completed\" });\n\n  for (const item of page.generations) {\n    console.log(item.id, item.contentUrl);\n  }\n\n  while (page.hasMore) {\n    page = await elevenlabs.flows.image.list({\n      pageSize: 20,\n      status: \"completed\",\n      cursor: page.nextCursor,\n    });\n    for (const item of page.generations) {\n      console.log(item.id, item.contentUrl);\n    }\n  }\n  ```\n\u003c/CodeBlocks\u003e\n\n`page_size` accepts 1 to 100 and defaults to 30. Pass `status` to return only generations in one\nlifecycle state, and `model_id` to return only generations of a single model.
